title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
mechanism: Average weights of models fine-tuned from one shared init with different hyperparameters; greedy soup chosen on held-out data.
adaptation: Our seeds share only the ImageNet encoder; decoders are random per seed, so fork 5 continuations from one checkpoint at 2k-5k steps (different seeds, aug order, Dice weights), uniform and greedy soup on F51 + val, recompute BN.
min_experiment: Step 0 (free): average 5 existing PF seeds, eval on val (expected collapse). Arm: forked soup (k=4k), 2 replicates. Baseline: same forks as output ensemble and as singles. Metric: crack IoU on CV / clean 49. Kill: soup below mean single of its members.
evidence: R: ImageNet, WILDS and text classification gains without inference cost; no segmentation results.
prior_overlap: none run; a soup of 5 PF seeds was proposed 30 Oct and not run
